scope-2002: SHARING clause of a sequential, relative or indexed file control entry sets the sharing mode unless the OPEN SHARING phrase overrides it
whether record locks have an effect (no other: ignored; read only / all other: in effect), per 9.1.14 and Table 20

evidence-2002.record locks in effect under SHARING WIT: covered by probe shlock.cob at --std 2002 (READ2-LOCKED=51, other record 00)

citations.quote: The SHARING clause specifies the sharing mode to be used for the file unless it is overridden
The SHARING clause specifies the sharing mode to be used for the file unless it is overridden
Additionally, the sharing mode for the current OPEN statement shall permit all of the sharing modes

cases.reason: Only the cross-reference number differs (9.1.14 vs 9.1.15). 2002 Table 20 is cell for cell 2023 Table 19; the 2002-only 'Additionally ...' sentence is what the table's SHARING WITH NO OTHER / READ ONLY rows already encode. 2023's 9.1.15 adds only APPLY COMMIT lock-release cases, a facility 2002 lacks. The SHARING general format is identical; the LOCK MODE requirement with ALL OTHER is in both OPEN statements. No CD reach.

cases.reason: The 2002 rule defers to ALL of 14.7, whose own text scopes the conformance check to activations by the CALL on-overflow format: 2002 14.7 NOTE 2 lists 'the on-overflow and on-exception formats of the CALL statement' (runtime check, EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH), and 2002 CALL GR3d applies 14.7 to all three 2002 CALL formats, after which GR3g1 transfers a mismatch to the ON OVERFLOW imperative. 2023 SR3 points only to 14.8.2/14.8.3, and 2023 14.8.1 NOTE 2 names only 'the Program format of the CALL statement'; CALL ON OVERFLOW is removed in 2023 (the compiler refuses it at --std 2023, COBOL0882). So part of the 2002 scope (linkage parameters conforming to arguments of a CALL ... ON OVERFLOW, mismatch routed to the overflow branch) has no evidence through the 2023 row. Probe ovfarg.cob (X(3) argument, X(5) formal, >>TURN EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH CHECKING ON): --std 2002 prints OVERFLOW-TAKEN / AFTER-CALL (correct per §2002:14.8.4.3 GR3d and GR3g); --std 2023 refuses. Control excarg.cob (ON EXCEPTION) behaves the same at both. Needs: a 2002 witness for the ON OVERFLOW case (ovfarg.cob is the candidate); compiler-at-2002 correct.

cases.reason: The rule makes report items 'obey the syntax rules and general rules defined for each clause' of USAGE, PICTURE, BLANK WHEN ZERO and JUSTIFIED: a deferral to the PICTURE clause, whose rules differ. 2002 limits character-string-1 to 50 characters; 2023 to 63. 2002 limits every numeric-edited item, floating-point edited included, to 31 digit positions; 2023 allows a 36-digit significand. So a 2002 report item with a 51-63 character picture is forbidden by this rule in 2002 and allowed by its 2023 twin. The 2023 row's evidence (BWZ / JUSTIFIED / USAGE / SIGN refusals) cannot show the 2002 limit. Probe rppic55.cob (report item PIC of 55 X's): --std 2002 refused COBOL2146 'maximum is 50 at COBOL-2002'; --std 2023 compiles and prints HELLO into the report. Compiler correct at 2002; the row needs its own 2002 witness (rppic55.cob is the candidate; the 31-digit floating-point edited limit in a report item is not yet probed).
